blocks.text: CEBU CITY, Philippines — Metro Cebu’s air pollution can linger near the ground due to weak winds and a weather phenomenon called temperature inversion. Environmental and weather officials said these conditions keep pollutants from dispersing, worsening the impact of emissions from vehicles, industries, and other local sources. The Metro Cebu monitoring station recorded an air quality index (AQI) of 156 at 7 a.m. on Thursday, October 15, keeping air quality in the “very unhealthy” category, according to the Environmental Management Bureau Region 7 (EMB-7).
